free_tier.stated: Quoted: 'The free plan never expires', 'no credit card needed', 'Free subdomain for every server', 'Unmetered bandwidth on every plan'. The live panel mock on the home page shows 'CPU 0.3 vCPU', 'Memory 74 / 256 MB', 'Disk 120 / 512 MB'.

per_object_cap.stated: not published as a count: the free plan is described per server (0.3 vCPU, 256 MB RAM, 512 MB disk) and no page read states how many free servers an account may hold

retention.stated: The free plan is time-limited and renewed by hand. Quoted: 'The server runs for a limited time. Before it expires, complete a short advertising or link flow to extend its uptime. This funds the free plan.' The renewal options default to '12 or 24 hours', each usable 'once per renewal window', with a default window of 24 hours.

interface_detail: a dashboard with a live console that accepts input, a file manager, and a free subdomain per server; seven runtimes (Node.js, Python, PHP, Bun, Java, C#, Rust)
tooling: the vendor dashboard; no SSH and no root
chaining: A small long-running process with a public subdomain, kept alive by a browser flow every 12 to 24 hours. Useful only where a human or a browser can do that flow, which rules out a fully unattended node.

limits.value: the free server expires unless an advertising or link flow is completed, with 12 or 24 hour renewal options
0.3 vCPU, 256 MB RAM, 512 MB disk per free server
a link or advertising flow must be completed to extend uptime

binding_note: The machine does not survive unattended: its lifetime is measured in 12 or 24 hour blocks that a link or advertising flow has to renew, so a tab closed for a day ends the machine.

identity_cost.detail: no card: quoted 'no credit card needed' on the signup page. the page states only that an account is created. Paid plans require the user to be at least 18.

reliability_note: The vendor status page at status.hokas.net reported 'All services are online' with 'Last updated on Oct 24, 2026 at 4:05am UTC', read today. That is the vendor's own measurement.
confidence_note: The renewal mechanics and the free plan's limits are quoted from the vendor's own documentation read today. The exact free allocation is taken from the panel mock on the marketing page rather than from a plan table, which is weaker, and the signup form's fields were not read.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'Free plan: There is no charge. The server runs for a limited time. Before it expires, complete a short advertising or link flow to extend its uptime. This funds the free plan.'

quoted: 'If no custom duration is set, the options are 12 or 24 hours'; 'Complete the short link flow that opens. When you return, the duration is added to your server.'; 'You can use each duration option once per renewal window. The default window is 24 hours.'
quoted: 'The free plan never expires', 'Paid plans are optional', 'CPU 0.3 vCPU', 'Memory 74 / 256 MB', 'Disk 120 / 512 MB'
quoted: 'Free plan that never expires, no credit card needed'; 'Free subdomain for every server'; 'Unmetered bandwidth on every plan'
quoted: 'All services are online', 'Last updated on Oct 24, 2026 at 4:05am UTC'

notes: Recorded because it is the clearest example of a free tier whose marketing says 'never expires' while its own documentation says the server 'runs for a limited time' and is renewed by completing an advertising or link flow in 12 or 24 hour blocks. The contradiction is the finding: the marketing sentence and the documentation sentence are both on the vendor's own site, read today. That renewal loop is a human action, so the machine does not survive a tab closing, which is the bar set. Everything else about it is reasonable: a real dashboard, seven runtimes, a free subdomain, unmetered bandwidth, no card.

extras.term: 12 or 24 hour blocks, renewed by a link or advertising flow

network_out.ports: a free subdomain per server; port list not published

session_cap.note: 12 or 24 hours per renewal, and each option is usable once per 24-hour window, so the practical maximum is 24 hours of uptime per renewal
